Using binary potential outcomes $(Y(0),Y(1))$, persuadables are (0,1), sure things (1,1), lost causes (0,0), and sleeping dogs (1,0). Both potential outcomes are never observed for the same person in an ordinary experiment, so these are conceptual types, not directly identifiable customer labels. The learnable target is usually conditional average treatment effect. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

An S-learner fits one outcome model using features and treatment; a T-learner fits separate treated/control models and subtracts predictions. An X-learner imputes individual treatment effects using those models, fits effect models within each group, then combines them using weights often related to propensity. Compare on randomized held-out data using policy value or uplift metrics, with uncertainty and capacity constraints. Strong outcome prediction alone does not imply reliable treatment-effect ranking.
